title: Nexus
description: Full-stack project management application with authentication, task tracking, Kanban board, and analytics. Built with Next.js App Router, Server Actions, and Prisma.

caseStudy.projectOverview: Nexus is a full-stack project management application built with Next.js 15 App Router. It covers authentication (Google OAuth + email/password), task and project management, a Kanban board, and an analytics dashboard with charts. The project started as a client-only frontend consuming an external REST API and has since been fully migrated to a server-first architecture using Server Components, Server Actions, and Prisma ORM.
caseStudy.problemPurpose: The goal was to build a production-grade application that goes beyond visual polish, addressing data architecture, server-side rendering, type-safe mutations, and authentication in a single cohesive Next.js project. It also served as a real migration exercise: replacing a separate backend, React Query, and Axios with Next.js built-in capabilities.
myFocus: Migrating from a client-side API-consuming frontend to a fullstack Next.js architecture with Server Components and Server Actions
Implementing Auth.js v5 with Google OAuth and email/password credentials, including password reset with email verification and rate limiting
Designing a type-safe Server Actions pattern with centralised ActionResult types and Zod validation
Building a co-located component and action architecture with per-feature subfolders and unit tests
whyThisStack: Next.js App Router enables Server Components and Server Actions, eliminating the need for a separate API layer and client-side state management library
Prisma ORM provides type-safe database access that integrates cleanly with TypeScript and keeps schema and queries in sync
Auth.js v5 handles the full authentication lifecycle (sessions, OAuth, and credentials) with Edge-compatible middleware for route protection
Zod ensures consistent validation across Server Actions and form inputs, with errors surfaced to the UI in a uniform pattern
keyFeatures: Google OAuth and email/password authentication with password reset flow and rate limiting
IDOR protection on all database queries, with every query scoped by userId
Task management with filtering, pagination, tagging, and status tracking
Analytics dashboard with priority distribution and tasks-by-status charts
Dark and light theme with mobile-responsive layout and drawers
Reusable Server Actions with centralised ActionResult type and Zod validation
challengesTradeoffs: Migrating incrementally from React Query and Axios to Server Actions without breaking existing features
Designing a scalable actions architecture, splitting monolithic files into co-located per-action modules with tests
Balancing server-side simplicity with client interactivity using the 'use client' boundary carefully
whatILearned: Server Components significantly reduce client bundle size and remove the need for explicit loading state management in most cases
Co-locating actions and tests in per-feature subfolders makes the codebase easier to navigate and reduces friction when adding tests
A centralised ActionResult type with consistent Zod validation across all Server Actions prevents a whole class of runtime errors
nextSteps: Add E2E tests with Playwright covering the auth flow and critical user paths
Implement saved views, recurring tasks, and subtask support
Add email digest and keyboard shortcut support
Explore SaaS foundations: multi-user workspaces and billing

title: Brev.ly
description: Full-stack URL shortener with link management, access tracking, and CSV export via Cloudflare R2. Built with React, Fastify, and PostgreSQL — deployed to AWS S3 + CloudFront.

caseStudy.projectOverview: Brev.ly is a full-stack URL shortening platform built as a monorepo with a React + Vite frontend and a Fastify + PostgreSQL API. It covers the full product lifecycle — from link creation and redirection to access tracking, CSV export via Cloudflare R2, and automated deployment to AWS S3 + CloudFront via GitHub Actions.
caseStudy.problemPurpose: Most URL shorteners are either too basic or overloaded with unnecessary features. The goal was to build a focused, production-ready core experience — with clean validation, reliable state handling, and an infrastructure that could scale.
myFocus: Designing a clean and reliable link creation and management flow with strong validation
Implementing real-time access count sync across browser tabs using BroadcastChannel
Building a CSV export pipeline using Cloudflare R2 for CDN-accessible file delivery
Setting up a full CI/CD pipeline with GitHub Actions deploying to AWS S3 + CloudFront
whyThisStack: Fastify provides a fast, lightweight API layer well-suited to a focused backend with clear route responsibilities
Drizzle ORM keeps database interactions type-safe and aligned with the TypeScript codebase
React Query handles server state and caching cleanly, reducing manual loading and error management
Cloudflare R2 offers CDN-backed file storage for CSV exports without the cost overhead of S3 for static assets
keyFeatures: Short URL generation with validation and duplicate prevention
Access count tracking with real-time sync across tabs via BroadcastChannel
Infinite scroll using IntersectionObserver for paginated link loading
CSV export stored on Cloudflare R2 and accessible via CDN
Automated CI/CD pipeline via GitHub Actions → AWS S3 + CloudFront
challengesTradeoffs: Defining the right MVP scope to protect delivery speed without sacrificing product quality
Managing real-time state across browser tabs without introducing unnecessary complexity
Structuring the monorepo so client and server remain independent but easy to develop together
whatILearned: BroadcastChannel is a simple and effective solution for cross-tab state sync without external libraries
A well-scoped MVP with solid validation foundations is easier to extend than a broad one with weak contracts
Automating deployment early removes friction and builds confidence throughout the development process
